questions.q: What is the minimum acceptable slope for water drainage away from a structure on a paver patio?
questions.explanation: The industry-standard minimum for paver drainage away from any structure is 1/8 inch per foot — enough to shed water without being visually noticeable.

questions.q: Base rock for pavers should be laid and compacted in what lift depth?
questions.explanation: Two-inch lifts, each plate-compacted separately, give the densest and most predictable base. Anything thicker leaves under-compacted material that will settle later.

questions.q: Bedding sand for pavers should be what depth after screeding?
questions.explanation: One inch of coarse washed concrete sand, uncompacted, is the industry standard. Thicker bedding sand is one of the most common causes of wave patterns showing up months later.

questions.q: Which pattern is best for a driveway that will see regular vehicle traffic?
questions.explanation: 45-degree herringbone locks pavers against each other in two directions, resisting rutting from turning wheels far better than running bond or basketweave.

questions.q: Why should paver cutting always be wet-cut with a diamond blade?
choices: Dry cutting creates hazardous silica dust
Diamond blades only work when wet
questions.explanation: Cutting concrete or stone pavers dry releases respirable crystalline silica dust, which is a serious health hazard. Wet cutting suppresses the dust.

questions.q: What is the primary risk of using standard mason sand instead of coarse washed concrete sand for the bedding layer?
choices: Mason sand compacts and holds moisture, causing settling and freeze/thaw damage
questions.explanation: Coarse concrete sand drains freely and stays stable under load. Mason sand is finer, holds water, and compacts unpredictably — a leading cause of premature paver failure.

questions.q: How long should you typically wait after installation before sealing pavers?
questions.explanation: Fresh pavers release efflorescence for weeks. Sealing traps the efflorescence under the film. Waiting 60-90 days lets it clear so the sealer bonds properly.

questions.q: A paver has settled a quarter inch below its neighbors. What is the correct repair approach?
choices: Sweep joint sand into the gap around it
Lift the paver, add bedding sand, and reset it
Ignore it — the customer won't notice
questions.explanation: Settled pavers are lifted, the underlying void is corrected with fresh bedding sand or base rock as needed, and the paver is reset. Filling the gap only hides the failure.

questions.q: Polymeric joint sand should be activated with:
choices: A garden hose set to fine mist per the product's directions
Nothing — it activates from air moisture
questions.explanation: Polymeric sand needs controlled, light watering per the product's directions. Too little water and it stays powdery; too much floats the polymer to the surface as a haze.

questions.q: During excavation, if your boot sinks a quarter inch into the subgrade when you stomp, what should you do?
choices: Proceed — the base rock will bridge it
Dig deeper to firmer material, or add geotextile fabric
Compact the soft subgrade with a plate compactor
questions.explanation: Soft subgrade is a failure point that base rock alone won't solve — the base migrates into the soft material over time. Dig deeper to stable ground or install geotextile fabric to isolate the layers.

questions.q: The recommended waste factor when ordering pavers is:
questions.explanation: 10-15% waste covers cuts, breakage during install, and a small stock of matching pavers for future warranty repairs — critical because color lots shift year to year.

questions.q: Edge restraint should be spiked into the base rock at what spacing?
questions.explanation: One spike per foot is the industry-standard spacing that holds the perimeter stiff against normal freeze/thaw movement and traffic loading.
